2. The case of the petitioner in brief is as under:
a.
The marriage between the petitioner and the respondent was solemnized on 14.07.2005 at Shivanubhava Kalyana Mantapa, Sri Hukkeri Mata, Haveri, as per Hindu rites and customs.
It was an arranged marriage, conducted in the presence of both families and well-wishers.

The petitioner's parents provided gold ornaments,
silver articles, and cash as dowry to the respondent as per his demand.

The couple has three children: 1) Pavan R.H., studying II PUC at Sri Chaitanya PU College,
Rajajinagar, 2) Kum. Pooja R.H., studying in 7th Std. at Sarodaya National Public School, and 3) Pranav R.H., Crl.Misc.No.232/2023 JUDGMENT studying in 2nd Std.
at JSS High School, Suttur Mata, Mysore.
The petitioner states that the respondent has been irresponsible and never showed love or affection towards her after marriage.
He subjected her to constant mental and physical harassment, making unfounded allegations against her character and her family.

After the birth of their third child, the respondent began to accuse the petitioner of infidelity, claiming that Smt Bharati R Hiremath vs Sri Renukayya C Hiremath @ Renukaswamy on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17027193/

sentences.text: the third child was not his.
Under duress, the petitioner underwent a paternity test for all three children on 27.12.2017, which confirmed that the respondent is the father of all three children.
Despite this, the respondent continued to deny his parental responsibilities, refusing to pay the school fees for the third child, Pranav.

Due to financial constraints, the petitioner had to admit him to Suttur Mata.
b.
The respondent's behavior caused immense mental agony to the petitioner, and he often insulted her in front of the children and relatives using abusive language.
The respondent also frequently quarreled with her over trivial matters and made disparaging remarks about her character.
His disrespectful Crl.Misc.No.232/2023 JUDGMENT attitude, coupled with threats of violence and cruel behavior, made it impossible for the petitioner to continue living with him.
Additionally, the respondent's chronic alcoholism further contributed to the cruelty.
c. The petitioner has also suffered physical harm due to the respondent's assaults, which resulted in damage to her eardrum and the need for surgery.
She claims that the constant mental torture and physical abuse caused her to suffer from depression.

Despite the respondent's significant income,
including earnings from his profession as an advocate and immovable properties worth over Rs.
2,00,000 per month, he has neglected his duties to maintain the petitioner and their children.
d. After being thrown out by the respondent in June 2023, the petitioner now resides separately with her children in a rented house.

She works as a tailor, earning a meager salary of Rs. 11,000 per month, which is insufficient to cover her basic living expenses, including food, shelter, medical bills,
and the children's school fees.
The elders from both families attempted Crl.Misc.No.232/2023 JUDGMENT to resolve the issues through several panchayats, but the respondent refused to cooperate.

The petitioner further states that the respondent has threatened her with dire consequences for not bringing additional dowry and has even claimed to possess photographs and videos that would tarnish her reputation.

e. Unable to bear the constant abuse, the petitioner filed a complaint against the respondent with the Vijayanagar Police, leading to the registration of a case under Crime No. 200/2003, dated 17-06-2003, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, and 506 of the IPC.
Therefore, the petitioner prays that the petition be allowed.
3. After the registration of the petition, notices were issued to the respondent in accordance with the legal procedure.
The notices were duly served to the respondent.

However, despite proper service,
the respondent failed to appear before the Court on the scheduled dates.
As a result of the respondent's failure to attend the proceedings and participate Crl.Misc.No.232/2023 JUDGMENT in the case, the Court took the necessary step of placing the respondent ex-parte.
Subsequently, the matter was set down for trial, and the proceedings continued in the respondent's absence.
4. To substantiate her case, the petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.8 and closed her side.

sentences.text: With these observations, this Court answers the point No.1 in the Affirmative.
Crl.Misc.No.232/2023 JUDGMENT 11. Point No.2 :
As discussed above, the petitioner has successfully established that she has been subjected to cruelty by the respondent and has been deserted by him.

The petitioner has contended that the respondent has failed to provide any financial support or make arrangements for her and her children's residence, despite his legal obligation as her husband and the father of their children.

The petitioner has further alleged that the respondent is a practicing advocate and owns several immovable properties in different locations, including Ranebennur, Byloconahalli, Belagavi,
Chikkodi, Channapattana, and Kadamanahalli Village.
The petitioner claims that the respondent earns approximately Rs. 2,00,000 per month from his profession and the income generated from his properties.

To substantiate these claims, the petitioner has produced several key documents in support of her assertions:
1.Ex.P.4 and Ex.P.5:
These documents consist of welfare fund receipts paid by the respondent to the Karnataka State Bar Council, along with details of his membership with the Bar Council.

These Crl.Misc.No.232/2023 JUDGMENT receipts demonstrate that the respondent has been practicing law in Karnataka since 2003,
confirming his professional standing as a lawyer.
The petitioner has relied on these documents to establish that the respondent's legal profession is a stable source of income.
2.Ex.P.6 and Ex.P.7:
These are the record of rights for two agricultural properties owned by the respondent.
The first property, bearing Sy. No. 26/2A, is located at Kadamanahalli, Taluk Byadagi, District Haveri, and measures 2 acres 29 guntas.

The second property, bearing Sy. No. 83/2B, is situated at Devarahosahalli, Taluk Channapatna,
District Ramanagara, and measures 1 acre 11 guntas.
Both records of rights indicate that the respondent is the owner of these properties.
This further substantiates the petitioner's claim that the respondent has significant immovable assets and, by extension, a stable income source.
Crl.Misc.No.232/2023 JUDGMENT 12.
Upon an appreciation of Ex.P.4 to Ex.P.7, it is evident that the respondent is a successful lawyer with a flourishing practice.
Additionally, the respondent's purchase of agricultural land using the income from his legal profession highlights his financial capability.
This establishes that the respondent has sufficient income to support his family but has failed to fulfill his obligation to maintain his wife and children.
13. After thoroughly considering all the material on record, it is abundantly clear that the petitioner and her children are currently residing separately from the respondent.
Despite the respondent's legal obligation to maintain his wife and children, he has failed to do so.

As the husband and father,

sentences.text: the respondent bears the legal responsibility to provide maintenance for the petitioner and their children.

While the petitioner works as a tailor and earns a modest income of Rs. 11,000 per month,
this amount is insufficient to meet the needs of herself and her children.
She is struggling to provide for the basic necessities such as food, clothing, shelter, medical care, and educational expenses for her children.
Crl.Misc.No.232/2023 JUDGMENT 14.
The petitioner has made it clear that, due to the insufficient income from her work, she is facing significant financial hardship in supporting herself and her children.
Her income is inadequate for sustaining their day-to-day life, and the family is struggling to make ends meet.
This situation has caused immense stress and has made it impossible for her to maintain a dignified life without financial support.
15. Taking into account the facts of the case and the respective financial positions of the parties, this Court finds that the petitioner is entitled to compensation and maintenance.
The respondent's failure to support his family, despite his substantial income from his legal profession and immovable properties, is inexcusable.
In light of the emotional distress, financial hardship, and mental anguish caused by the respondent's actions, the Court has decided to grant compensation to the petitioner.
16. Thus, this Court awards the petitioner a compensation amount of Rs. 10,00,000 (Rupees Ten Lakhs Crl.Misc.No.232/2023 JUDGMENT only).
This compensation is intended to assist the petitioner in meeting her basic needs and to help mitigate the hardship and emotional distress caused by the respondent's cruelty and abandonment.
17. In addition to the compensation, the petitioner is entitled to monthly maintenance of Rs. 10,000 for herself.

Given the respondent's financial ability, he is also required to provide Rs. 4,000 per month for each of the minor children, to help support their basic needs and Rs. 40,000 per year towards the children's educational expenses until they attain the age of majority.
This will ensure that the children receive adequate education despite the financial constraints faced by the petitioner.

18. After considering the overall facts, the Court finds that the respondent's behavior has not only caused the petitioner significant emotional and physical distress but has also failed to fulfill his legal obligations as a husband and father.

The respondent's neglect has led to the petitioner's financial difficulties, and the Court is of the opinion that the Crl.Misc.No.232/2023 JUDGMENT compensation and maintenance ordered are necessary to address the immediate and ongoing needs of the petitioner and her children.
With these observations, this Court answers point No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
19. Point No.3 :

In view of discussion held above, this Court proceed to pass the following;
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner under Section 12 of Protection of Woman from Domestic Violence Act., is partly allowed.
